results.title: Semi-supervised recognition for artificial intelligence assisted ...
results.content: Therefore, the effective utilization of unlabeled medical image data and the design of semi-supervised semantic segmentation methods capable of handling this data complexity are important topics of current re-search. Research on semi-supervised semantic segmentation models is particularly active in the field of medical images. However, current semi-supervised learning models primarily focus on utilizing both labeled and unlabeled data to improve performance, without giving sufficient consideration to the spatial relationships between pixels. These enhancements allow our semi-supervised learning model to more effectively utilize the connections between pixels, resulting in improved segmentation accuracy. Fully supervised semantic segmentation models achieve semantic label assignment at the pixel level by learning from a large number of densely labeled images. By integrating the CRF module, our model can efficiently process image details and edge regions, resulting in improved segmentation performance. The introduction of RSAA enables the model to utilize spatial information more efficiently, improving its sensitivity to image details and ultimately enhancing segmentation accuracy.As the proportion of labels increases, the mIoU scores of all models improve.
